questions.q: A real-time system is one whose correctness depends on:
options: Only the speed of the CPU
The logical result and the time it is produced
questions.explain: Correct but late is incorrect in a real-time system.

questions.q: Missing a deadline in an airbag controller is an example of a:
questions.explain: A missed hard deadline is system failure, possibly catastrophic.

questions.q: In a firm real-time system, a result produced after its deadline is:
options: Discarded because its value is zero
questions.explain: Firm: the late result is useless but the system does not fail.

questions.q: Which is the best example of a soft real-time system?
questions.explain: Occasional delays only lower quality.

questions.q: Which statement about embedded systems is true?
options: They perform a dedicated function within a larger system and need not have a time bound
They never interact with the real world
They are the same as real-time systems
questions.explain: Real-time emphasises timing; embedded emphasises a dedicated function.

questions.q: 'Real-time computing is the same as fast computing' is:
options: A common misconception: real-time means predictable
questions.explain: Real-time is about meeting deadlines predictably, not raw speed.

questions.q: An emergency stop with a known minimum time between presses and a hard deadline is a:
questions.explain: Sporadic: irregular but with a minimum inter-arrival time.

questions.q: A constraint imposed on the stimuli produced by the environment is a:
questions.explain: Behavioural constraints make sure the environment is well behaved.

questions.q: Safety-critical systems guarantee safety mainly through:
questions.explain: They have no fail-safe state, so reliability must be very high.

questions.q: In TMR, a single faulty module is masked by:
questions.explain: Three modules, two-out-of-three vote.

questions.q: Software fault tolerance is harder than hardware fault tolerance mainly because:
options: Failures of software versions are statistically correlated
questions.explain: Versions fail for the same reasons; hardware faults are independent.

questions.q: A primary module, an acceptance test and alternate modules describe:
questions.explain: If the acceptance test fails, an alternate is tried.

questions.q: Which architecture has a single point of failure?
questions.explain: One controller does everything.

questions.q: In a hierarchical control system, the strictest real-time deadlines are handled at the:
questions.explain: The lower level does fast local control of sensors and actuators.

questions.q: Changing a sensor's bipolar output into the 0–5 V range of an ADC without changing its shape is:
questions.explain: Level shifting moves the signal into the accepted range.

questions.q: For accurate measurement of encoder pulses, the preferred method is:
questions.explain: Hardware capture avoids missed pulses and jitter.

questions.q: Which I/O type carries information in pulse width, frequency or count?
questions.explain: Pulse I/O: PWM, encoders, flow meters.

questions.q: A signal has a maximum frequency of 250 Hz. What is the minimum (Nyquist) sampling frequency in Hz?
questions.explain: $f_s \ge 2f_{max} = 500$ Hz.

questions.q: The variation in sampling or execution timing is called:
questions.explain: Jitter distorts samples; RTOS and hardware timers reduce it.

questions.q: Sampling all channels at the same instant is:
questions.explain: Needed for multi-lead ECG or three-phase measurements.

questions.q: Which should NOT be done inside an ISR?
questions.explain: An ISR must never wait indefinitely for a resource.

questions.q: The data structure holding a task's priority, state and saved registers is the:
questions.explain: The TCB lets the scheduler suspend and resume tasks.

questions.q: In a clock-driven scheduler, scheduling points are:
questions.explain: Event-driven ones use events; hybrid ones use both.

questions.q: Three tasks have $(C, T)$ of $(1, 4)$, $(2, 6)$ and $(1, 10)$ ms. What is the total utilisation $U$? Give 3 decimal places.
What is the Liu and Layland utilisation bound for $n = 3$ tasks? Give 3 decimal places.
Under rate monotonic scheduling, the highest priority goes to the task with the:
questions.explain: Fixed priority, inversely proportional to the period.

questions.q: A task set has $U = 0.80$ with three tasks. Under RM it is:
options: Not guaranteed by the bound; check with response-time analysis
questions.explain: The Liu and Layland test is sufficient, not necessary.

questions.q: On one processor with $D_i = T_i$, EDF schedules a task set if and only if:
questions.explain: EDF is optimal on a uniprocessor.

questions.q: Under EDF overload, tasks miss their deadlines one after another. This is the:
questions.explain: Transient overload causes a cascade of misses.

questions.q: T1 = (1, 4), T2 = (2, 6), T3 = (3, 8). What is $U$? Give 3 decimal places.
Tasks have periods 4, 5 and 20. What is the major cycle (hyperperiod)?
Which is the cyclic scheduler's constraint that a full frame lies between release and deadline?
questions.explain: Constraint 3.

questions.q: P1 (5, arrives 0), P2 (4, 1), P3 (2, 2), P4 (1, 4), quantum 2 ms. What is the average waiting time in ms?
questions.explain: Waiting times 7, 6, 2, 4; average 19/4 = 4.75 ms.

questions.q: Which statement about non-pre-emptive scheduling is true?
options: A task runs to completion once started
questions.explain: Less overhead but lower schedulability.

questions.q: A semaphore used for a pool of five identical printers should be a:
questions.explain: A counting semaphore covers N identical resources.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four necessary conditions for deadlock?
questions.explain: The condition is *no* pre-emption.

questions.q: With one instance per resource, deadlock exists if the wait-for graph:
options: Has a process with no edges
questions.explain: A closed loop of waits is deadlock.

questions.q: The Banker's algorithm grants a request only if:
options: The system remains in a safe state
The process has the highest priority
questions.explain: It is a deadlock avoidance algorithm.

questions.q: Unbounded priority inversion is caused when a high-priority task waits for a low one and:
options: A medium-priority task pre-empts the low one
questions.explain: M keeps L from releasing the lock.

questions.q: Which protocol may refuse a request for a FREE resource?
questions.explain: PCP is not greedy; it denies requests at or below the current system ceiling.

questions.q: CAN bus arbitration gives the bus to the message with the:
questions.explain: Bitwise, non-destructive arbitration: dominant 0 bits win.

questions.q: The Internet is suitable in real-time systems mainly for:
questions.explain: It cannot guarantee bounded delay.

questions.q: A protocol in which a single frame passes through all nodes and each reads or writes on the fly is:
questions.explain: This gives microsecond synchronization.

questions.q: In which communication model does the producer not need to know who consumes the data?
questions.explain: A broker decouples publishers and subscribers.

questions.q: The most suitable process model for an anti-lock braking controller is:
questions.explain: It is safety-critical with stable requirements.

questions.q: Which protocol combines a time-triggered static segment with an event-triggered dynamic segment?
questions.explain: FlexRay is hybrid and uses a global clock.

questions.q: End-to-end delay in a real-time control chain is:
questions.explain: The whole chain must fit within the deadline.

questions.q: Testing a real controller connected to a computer simulation of the plant is:
questions.explain: HIL: real hardware plus a simulated environment.

questions.q: Checking that a base station stays stable when many users call at once is:
questions.explain: Stress testing applies extreme load.

questions.q: WirelessHART and 5G URLLC are examples of:
questions.explain: Timing is guaranteed by scheduled access.
